title: Genetic evidence that the human CYP2R1 enzyme is a key vitamin D 25-hydroxylase
authors: Cheng JB, Levine MA, Bell NH, Mangelsdorf DJ, Russell DW
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
funder: Robert A. Welch Foundation Grants I-0971 and I-1275; National Institutes of Health Grants HL 20948, GM 08014 and DK 56603; and the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.
result: Synthesis of active vitamin D requires 25-hydroxylation in the liver and 1α-hydroxylation in the kidney, the latter by the mitochondrial enzyme CYP27B1. A patient with low circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D and classic symptoms of vitamin D deficiency was homozygous for a transition in exon 2 of CYP2R1 on chromosome 11p15.2 that substitutes proline for a conserved leucine at residue 99 and eliminated vitamin D 25-hydroxylase activity. One of 50 Nigerian control subjects was heterozygous for the same L99P change.
